value.title: Paired-output binary-table curvature proof
value.summary: For an arbitrary input law on the two-letter half-skew BSSC, memorylessness maps the input covariance c_in to covariance c_in/4 in each receiver's binary output table. Along each fixed-marginal covariance segment, differentiating binary relative entropy twice and pairing the two receiver tables yields a uniform reciprocal-curvature lower bound. Integrating twice from independence proves I(Y_1;Y_2)+I(Z_1;Z_2) >= 31 c_in^2/(20 ln 2), including boundary and degenerate cases by continuity.

value.title: Directed paired-output curvature verifier
value.summary: A dependency-free Python standard-library checker verifies the exact paired-table reciprocal identities, the polynomial positivity and minimum bracket underlying the curvature constant, the rescaling from output covariance to input covariance, and directed logarithmic comparisons establishing sqrt(7 ln 2/248)<7/50. It corroborates but does not replace the analytic curvature proof.

value.title: Output curvature sharpens covariance pruning for a two-letter Marton gain
value.summary: Every input law on the half-skew BSSC product channel satisfies C_out=I(Y_1;Y_2)+I(Z_1;Z_2) >= 31 c_in^2/(20 ln 2), where c_in=P(X_1X_2=11)-P(X_1=1)P(X_2=1). Combining this unconditional curvature inequality with the accepted bound C_out<7/160 for any finite two-letter Marton law exceeding twice the optimal one-letter randomized-time-division value shows that every such gain requires |c_in|<sqrt(7 ln 2/248)<7/50. This necessary condition neither constructs nor rules out a gain, tensorizes Marton's functional, nor supplies a capacity converse.

placementAudit.rationale: The accepted result strengthens the covariance constraints required of any two-letter Marton gain, directly advancing the active non-root program's correlation-structure pruning objective.
